title: Ghunnah: noon and meem with shaddah: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Ash-Sharh, Ad-Duha 1 to 8 and applying the rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 31 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ghunnah rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 31. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Ghunnah: the nose sound
points: Every نّ and مّ has ghunnah
The sound comes from the nose (khayshum)

head: Not this
This
rows: Hold the hum for two counts: fa-in-na, thum-ma

keywords.def: a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
a mark: say the letter twice
the inside of the nose, where ghunnah comes from

questions.q: Read «فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا» (94:5) with a two-count ghunnah.
questions.a: fa-in-na ma'al-'usri yusraa: the نّ held two counts.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: circle every نّ and مّ in An-Nas and Al-Qadr, then read each with a two-count ghunnah. Today's rota group recites Ash-Sharh 1 to 3 to the teacher.
questions.a: An-Nas: ٱلنَّاسِ in 114:1 to 6 and ٱلْخَنَّاسِ; Al-Qadr: إِنَّآ (97:1).

questions.q: Extend: find the ghunnah in «إِنَّ مَعَ» (94:6).
Stretch: why do we hold ghunnah evenly every time?
questions.a: So the recitation is steady and correct, as the Prophet ﷺ was taught.

questions.q: How long is the ghunnah on نّ or مّ?
questions.a: A) Two counts. Ghunnah on a mushaddad noon or meem is held for two counts.

questions.q: Think again: Hold your nose and say 'nnn'. What happens? What does that tell you about where ghunnah comes from?
questions.a: The sound stops: ghunnah comes from the nose (al-khayshum).
